summary: Scoped prod eventstream access for EU customer data correction (timeboxed, least-privilege)
description:
Issue summary:
Support has received a request from EU enterprise customer 'NordicPay' to correct a handful of misattributed transaction IDs that were surfaced via user-visible inference output. Engineering needs timeboxed, least-privilege access to the production eventstream and related psql indexes to locate and verify the original requests and confirm redaction/correction.

Impact:
- Customer-facing data correction required to satisfy GDPR data rectification request.
- No production outage; business impact limited to customer trust and compliance risk if not completed within customer SLA.

Environment:
- prod, eu-west region (primary cluster: prod-eu-01)
- Components likely involved: event ingestion pipeline (kafka/eventstream), serving-runtime request logs, psql metadata indexes, auth/audit logs.

Requested scope and constraints:
- Timebox: 48 hours of access (proposed window: 2026-03-15 07:00 -- 2026-03-17 07:00 UTC).
- Data scope: 6 named request IDs and +/- 10 minutes around each event (to capture correlated metadata).
- Least-privilege: read-only access to a temporary view that joins eventstream offsets to request metadata; no bulk export of raw payloads.
- Crypto controls: any symmetric keys used to decrypt payloads must use dev-access KMS wrapper and audit log all decrypt calls.
- Redaction requirement: any non-essential PII must be redacted in any screenshots or extracts; only deterministic identifiers allowed in the analysis notes.

Steps to reproduce / deliverable expectations:
1) SRE/Infra to create a time-limited role (TTL 48h) with permission to query the eventstream materialized view and the psql request_index table for the six request_ids.
2) Support/Eng to run vetted queries from a predefined runbook (linked) and capture minimally necessary evidence.
3) Security to observe or receive live audit logs for the session and confirm no extra slices were requested.
4) After verification, Support to coordinate with Customer Success to confirm correction and produce a signed attestation for legal.

Why this is different from a normal log request:
- The customer is invoking GDPR Article 16-style rectification and requires authoritative mapping from visible inference output back to ingested events. This is a targeted, small-scope lookup rather than a broad log extract.

Approval checklist (requested):
- Legal signoff on scope and attestation language.
- Security signoff on temporary role and access review.
- SRE confirmation of the technical approach (temp view and no bulk export).

Related artifacts and references:
- Runbook: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/OPS/Targeted+Event+Lookup+Runbook
- Customer ticket: SUP-23841 (customer request thread)
- Incident page (for context): https://status.redwood.ai/incidents/2026-02-05-llm-output-mismatch
comments: Maya Thompson (2026-03-10): Filing formal internal request per customer legal team. Attached customer-signed rectification request. Asked for 48h window and strict read-only access to materialized view.
Ethan Cole (2026-03-11): SRE can create a scoped role and a temp view. Need Security to approve KMS access pattern. ETA to provision role: 8 hours after approval.

Priya Desai (Security) (2026-03-11): Can only approve if audit streaming is enabled for the session and key unwraps are logged to auditor. Also require Legal to confirm attestation language before any data is viewed.

Oliver Grant (Legal) (2026-03-12): Drafted attestation template and confirmed wording meets GDPR rectification requirements. Approve pending Security confirmation. Template link: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/LEGAL/GDPR+Attestation+Templates
Ethan Cole (2026-03-12): Updated provisioning checklist in PR #4127 to include auditor stream hookup and TTL enforcement. Awaiting final security sign-off to schedule window (suggest 2026-03-15).
investigation_notes: Checked eventstream retention policy: prod-eu-01 retains offsets for 14 days, sufficient for requested window.
Verified that request_index psql table contains an index on request_id; targeted queries are efficient and will not require table scans.
SRE verified that creating a materialized view that joins offsets to request metadata will not increase retention or create new replicas; materialized view will be ephemeral and dropped after TTL.
Security ran threat model: low risk if no write/export allowed and KMS unwraps are auditable in real time.
resolution: Pending approvals from Security and Legal. Technical provisioning plan prepared by SRE (PR linked). If approved, provisioning and verification will be completed within the requested 48h window; final attestation will be issued to Customer Success for delivery to customer.
resolution_status_notes: Approvals outstanding as of 2026-03-12: Security approval of live audit stream confirmed; Legal attestation template approved; awaiting Security confirmation of KMS audit endpoint readiness and scheduling for proposed window.
